thesis: The surah's close widens Yusuf into the universal prophetic pattern — messengers were human men from real towns, help arrives at the edge of extremity, and the stories are 'ibrah rather than entertainment — and the despair of 12:110 is despair of the audience, not of Allah.
notes: REPAIR FULLY CONFIRMED against the fetched editions, clause by clause. (1) COUNT: 'Three of the four' is correct. al-Tabari supplies the object verbatim — 'حتى إذا استيأس الرسل ... أن يؤمنوا بالله ويصدقوهم فيما أتوهم به من عند الله' — which the file renders exactly. al-Muyassar: 'حتى إذا يئس الرسل من إيمان قومهم' — exact. al-Jalalayn gives ONLY the bare synonym: '﴿اسْتَيْأَسَ﴾ يَئِسَ ﴿الرُّسُل﴾' and moves straight to وظنوا — confirmed, it supplies no object. (2) IBN KATHIR'S CHAINS all three verified in the fetched text: Sa'id b. Jubayr ('when the Messengers gave up hope that their people will believe in them'); Ibn Mas'ud THROUGH Tamim b. Hadhlam (Ibn Kathir: 'Ibn Jarir At-Tabari narrated that Tamim bin Hadhlam said, I heard Abdullah bin Mas'ud comment on this Ayah ... that their people will believe in them'); Mujahid ('This is also the Tafsir that Mujahid bin Jabr and several other Salaf scholars gave'). (3) BUKHARI CHAIN exact: 'Al-Bukhari said that Urwah bin Az-Zubayr narrated that he asked Aishah'; her words 'Allah forbid! The Messengers did not suspect their Lord of such a thing'; she recited the tashdid ('Aishah recited this Ayah this way, وظنوا أنهم قد كُذِّبوا'); and the followers-reading is hers verbatim ('This Verse is concerned with the Messengers' followers ... suspected that even their followers were shaken in their belief'). (4) THE TWO RECITATIONS are represented exactly as al-Jalalayn has them: 'بالتشديد تكذيبا لا إيمان بعده والتخفيف أي ظن الأمم أن الرسل أُخلفوا ما وُعدوا به من النصر' — the file's two senses match word for word. Ibn Kathir's quoted sentence ('there is another way of reciting this word, and there is a difference of opinion about its meaning') is verbatim. (5) 'Al-Tabari gathers dozens of these reports, states which recitation he prefers and why, and records A'ishah's objection' — verified: al-Tabari says 'وإنما اخترنا هذا التأويل وهذه القراءة، لأن...' and separately 'وقد ذُكِر هذا التأويل ... لعائشة، فأنكرته أشد النكرة' with the معاذ الله report. (6) Ibn Kathir's split ('some referred that thought to the believing followers, and some to the disbelievers of the nation') is quoted almost verbatim from the fetched text. ADAB ('isma): the new section reports and enumerates, names the qira'ah dispute as the locus, does not adjudicate, and explicitly defers ('This reflection does not settle any of that ... For that, ask a qualified scholar'). No new overclaim introduced; no countable claims elsewhere in the file to break.

thesis: After argument has been exhausted, the Prophet is told to place the dispute before Allah as witness between both parties, and Khabir/Basir is what makes that witness complete — comforting the sincere and exposing the self-deceived.
notes: REPAIR CONFIRMED at all four edit sites. (1) The false two-sided attribution to al-Muyassar is GONE everywhere — grepped the whole file for Muyassar/'both sides'/'denial': the only two 'both sides' sentences (lines 108 and 182) now ground the reading in the Qur'anic wording (shahidan bayni wa-baynakum vs shahidan li) plus al-Tabari's al-muhiqq/al-mubtil, and no sentence anywhere still credits al-Muyassar with naming both sides. al-Muyassar's actual text confirms the original was false: 'كفى بالله شهيدا بيني وبينكم على صِدْقي وحقيقة نبوَّتي' — one side only, no takdhib clause. (2) The al-Tabari/al-Muyassar swap is untangled and both now match verbatim. al-Tabari 17:96: 'قل يا محمد للقائلين لك ﴿أبعث الله بشرا رسولا﴾ ... فإنه نعم الكافي والحاكم ... ذو خبرة وعلم بأمورهم وأفعالهم، والمحقّ منهم والمُبطل، والمُهدىّ والضالّ' — the file's rendering is exact, and the fabricated clause 'that I am His messenger to you' is gone. (3) Closing-clause attributions (line 142) all match: al-Tabari 'بصيرا بتدبيرهم وسياستهم وتصريفهم ... لا يخفى عليه شيء من أمورهم'; al-Muyassar 'خبير بأحوال عباده، بصير بأعمالهم، وسيجازيهم عليها'; Ibn Kathir as summarised. (4) Theme 2 now stands on the phrase itself and needs no attribution. NO new attribution invented — every added clause traces to fetched text. Note for the human, not a defect: al-Jalalayn (never cited in this file) independently supports section 5 — 'خبيرا بصيرا: عالما ببواطنهم وظواهرهم' — and glosses shahidan 'على صدقي', i.e. one-sided like al-Muyassar; the file correctly no longer leans on either for the two-sided reading. All nine Qur'anic cross-references verified against the Uthmani text (4:79, 4:166, 48:28, 13:43, 29:52, 10:71, 67:13-14, 40:19, and the 17:94-95 context).

thesis: Across 40:69-72 the six verbs predicated of the disputer alternate active/passive (active, passive — active, active — passive, passive), showing a man who never stops acting and never stops being acted upon; and the collar at the neck rhymes, by shared root motion, with the ghill carried in the chest.

flags.quote: On the dragging they agree: it is not metaphor but is done by hands, the *zabāniya*, the angels set over the punishment.
flags.issue: NEW breadth overclaim introduced by this repair — the exact defect class the rubric's binding rule names. The sentence's antecedent is 'The classical commentators' / the three editions just named (al-Muyassar, al-Jalalayn, al-Tabari), but al-Jalalayn names NO agent for the dragging. Its entire gloss is '﴿يُسْحَبُونَ﴾ أيْ يُجَرُّونَ بِها' — 'they are dragged BY THEM', i.e. by the chains, not by hands. Three of the four do carry it: al-Tabari 'يسحب هؤلاء ... زبانية العذاب يوم القيامة في الحميم'; al-Muyassar 'وتسحبهم زبانية العذاب'; Ibn Kathir 'the keepers of Hell will drag them along on their faces'. Per rubric rule 2, a silent edition is not an agreeing edition — and here al-Jalalayn is not merely silent, it supplies a different instrument. Fix: replace 'On the dragging they agree' with an enumeration, e.g. 'Three of the four make the dragging literal and put it in the hands of the zabaniya — al-Tabari, al-Muyassar and Ibn Kathir; al-Jalalayn glosses the verb only, yujarruna biha, dragged by the chains, and names no agent.'

flags.quote: The commentators are precise about the direction of that turning: *yuṣrafūn* is being turned away *from īmān*
flags.issue: Pre-existing (not introduced by this repair), but it is the same pattern and should be tightened while the file is open. Only al-Jalalayn says 'from iman' in those words: '﴿يُصْرَفُونَ﴾ عَنْ الإيمان'. al-Muyassar has 'كيف يعدلون عنها' (turned away from the signs), Ibn Kathir 'their minds are diverted from the truth', and al-Tabari does not gloss the direction at all. Naming al-Jalalayn would cost one clause and make it exact.

notes: The two named repairs THEMSELVES both check out; the failure is a third, new breadth claim introduced alongside repair (i). Repair (i) verified in every part: al-Muyassar does put the chains at the feet — 'تُجعل الأغلال في أعناقهم، والسلاسل في أرجلهم'; al-Jalalayn does offer it among options and its FIRST option is the necks coordination — '﴿والسلاسل﴾ عُطِفَ على الأغلال فتكون في الأعناق أو مبتدأ خبره محذوف أي في أرجلهم أو خبره ﴿يسحبون﴾'; and al-Tabari does adjudicate the qira'ah the other way and does invoke ijma' al-hujjah, verbatim: 'والصواب من القراءة عندنا فى ذلك ما عليه قراء الأمصار، لإجماع الحجة عليه، وهو رفع السلاسل عطفا بها على ما في قوله ﴿في أعناقهم﴾ من ذكر الأغلال.' Repair (ii) verified — al-Raghib al-Isfahani is now explicitly marked a lexicographer and his Mufradat placed outside the four tafsir editions. ALL PROTECTED COUNTS RE-CHECKED AND HOLD: root جدل appears exactly 5x in surah 40, at ayahs 4, 5, 35, 56, 69 — and surah 40 is uniquely highest (next are 4, 11 and 22 at 3 each). The six verbs predicated of these men and their voices are exactly as claimed — yujadiluna (IMPF, VF:3, active) and yusrafun (PASS) in 69; kadhdhabu (PERF, VF:2, active) and ya'lamun (IMPF, active) in 70; yushabun (PASS) in 71; yusjarun (PASS) in 72 — giving active/passive, active/active, passive/passive, with ya'lamun the only active verb still ahead of them. Also verified: aghlal at 40:71 is filed in the corpus under lemma غِلّ (so the file's 'a digital index files the two under one headword' is literally true); the clause 'ونزعنا ما في صدورهم من غل' occurs at exactly 7:43 and 15:47 and the two continuations are as described (rivers vs. brothers on couches); 40:56 'إن في صدورهم إلا كبر' and 40:73-74 'أين ما كنتم تشركون' / 'ضلوا عنا' verified. Clear the one moderate flag and this file passes.

thesis: Allah's help at Badr began inwardly — sleep, rain, purification, removal of Shaytan's whispering, hearts tied down, feet made firm — before it became outward victory and judgment, and the severity of 8:12 is framed by the cause named in 8:13.
notes: The 'of one mind' sentence was CHECKED EDITION BY EDITION as instructed, and it holds — all four gloss rijz inwardly as waswasa, none offers the outward/dirt reading in its own voice. al-Muyassar: 'ويزيل عنكم في الباطن وساوس الشيطان وخواطره' (explicitly في الباطن, and 'وساوس ... وخواطره' is exactly the file's 'the whispering, the passing thoughts'). al-Jalalayn: '﴿ويُذْهِب عَنْكُمْ رِجْز الشَّيْطان﴾ وسْوَسَته إلَيْكُمْ' — waswasatuhu, verbatim. Ibn Kathir: '(and to remove from you the Rijz of Shaytan,) such as his whispers and evil thoughts, this involves [inner] purification' — and he sets it against li-yutahhirakum as 'cleansing what is on the outside', which is precisely the pair the file describes. al-Tabari carries Mujahid twice — '﴿رجز الشيطان﴾ قال: وسوسته' and 'وساوسه' — and his own narrative frame reads it inwardly too ('وكان الشيطان قد وسوس إليهم ... فأذهب الله ذلك من قلوبهم بالمطر'). The file is careful to say 'the report al-Tabari carries from Mujahid', which is the honest form. So the replacement is NOT a new overclaim. Repair (ii) verified: al-Tabari's 'by the hands of My believing allies' sits under ayah 14, not the next verse — 'هذا العقابُ الذي عجلته لكم ... من الضرب فوق الأعناق منكم، وضرب كل بنان، بأيدي أوليائي المؤمنين' — so 'two verses later on ayah 14' is correct. Repair (iii) verified: al-Muyassar's gloss really is only 'كل طرف ومِفْصل' (every extremity and joint), and the sword-fight appositive is now clearly the file's own reading, not his — and it is independently corroborated by al-Jalalayn ('أطراف اليدين والرجلين'). 8:12 ADAB HOLDS AND IS STRONG: Badr framed as the specific engagement (al-Muyassar names 'غزوة بدر' verbatim); the addressee ikhtilaf is real and correctly reported (al-Muyassar inserts 'فاضربوا -أيها المؤمنون-', while Ibn Kathir reads the imperative as continuing to the angels, 'Allah then sent down to the angels ... so strike them over the necks', and also cites Ibn Jarir for the believers-address); and line 235 says outright 'they do not turn it into a standing instruction for a reader'. No truncation artifacts.

thesis: 11:44 compresses the whole cosmos into obedience — earth, sky, water, decree and resting-place all falling into place under a Commander the verse never names — and the only thing finally cast away is persistent zulm.
notes: Both repairs confirmed. (1) THE HEDGE IS NOW HONEST. 'This is one of the verses often named as a summit of the Qur'an's eloquence. That reputation is not something the commentators quoted below stop to argue — they move straight into explaining the scene' — I checked all four fetched editions and none of them raises balaghah at 11:44 at all: Ibn Kathir goes straight to the flood's end, al-Tabari to the ta'wil and the Judi reports, al-Muyassar and al-Jalalayn to bare paraphrase. So the file now asserts only what is true of them, and the reputation claim is reported rather than asserted as fact. (2) 'idha izdaradahu' IS al-Tabari's own wording, in his main text, not the editor's note: 'من قول القائل: بَلِعَ فلان كذا يَبْلَعُه، أو بَلَعَه يَبْلَعُه، إذا ازدَردَه.' The food-specific material (Ibn al-Qatta', 'بَلِعَ الطعام ... وبَلَعَ الماء') sits in the bracketed modern editor's footnote and is correctly no longer attributed to al-Tabari. PROTECTED STRUCTURAL CLAIMS RE-CHECKED AND ALL HOLD: 11:44 carries exactly 7 verbs — qila (PASS), ibla'i (IMPV), aqli'i (IMPV), ghida (PASS), qudiya (PASS), istawat (active), qila (PASS) — so exactly 4 passive, and the wa-qila frame is real (first verb and last verb of the ayah). The 'same three words' claim also holds: al-Tabari's ta'wil opens 'وقال الله للأرض بعد ما تناهى أمره في هلاك قوم نوح' and al-Muyassar opens 'وقال الله للأرض- بعد هلاك قوم نوح-' — the identical three-word opening, and it is also the source of the file's 'the command comes after Allah's affair had run its course'. Every other attribution verified verbatim: al-Tabari 'أقلعي عن المطر، أمسكي' and 'أي: تشرَّبي'; al-Muyassar 'اشربي ماءك', 'ونقص الماء ونَضَب', 'وقُضي أمر الله بهلاك قوم نوح', 'ورست السفينة على جبل الجودي', 'هلاكًا وبُعْدًا', 'الذين تجاوزوا حدود الله، ولم يؤمنوا به'; Ibn Kathir 'sprang from it and gathered upon it', 'it began to decrease'. 11:41 majraha/mursaha confirmed.

thesis: The seventh and last door of Ash-Shu'ara: the people of the Aykah answer Shu'ayb with a borrowed slur, a hunch dressed as a verdict, and a dare to drop the sky — and the sky answers as a canopy of shade that becomes fire, closing the surah's eight-fold refrain.
notes: AL-JALALAYN FETCH — REPORTING PLAINLY. The ar-tafsir-al-jalalayn endpoint 404s AGAIN for exactly 26:185 and 26:190 (the other five ayahs, 184/186/187/188/189, fetched fine and I read the file against them). This is not a transient failure: the whole-surah file ar-tafsir-al-jalalayn/26.json also has no entry for 185, 190 (or 191). I therefore pulled the same ayahs from two parallel Jalalayn editions on the same CDN (en-al-jalalayn and tafsir-al-jalalayn), both of which return the bare verse text with NO commentary for 26:185 and 26:190 — while returning full glosses for 184/186/187/189, matching the Arabic edition. Three independent signals agree: al-Jalalayn simply carries no gloss on those two ayahs. So the fourth edition HAS now been read for this file, and it contradicts nothing — 26:189 in fact corroborates the file's central scene almost word for word: 'عذاب يوم الظلة هي سحابة أظلتهم بعد حر شديد أصابهم فأمطرت عليهم نارا فاحترقوا' (a cloud that shaded them after severe heat, then rained fire and they burned). Human reviewer may wish to spot-check one printed Jalalayn for 26:185; my confidence that it is silent there is high but the ar- slug itself never returned. REPAIRS: (1) ARITHMETIC RE-COUNTED DIRECTLY, both numbers now correct and measuring the SAME span (the reply only, excluding qala): Arabic rabbi / a'lamu / bima / ta'malun = 4; the file's own English rendering 'My Lord knows best what you do' = My/Lord/knows/best/what/you/do = 7. The earlier reviewer's '6' was wrong. (2) 'unhinged by sorcery' is gone and Ibn Kathir's quote is now verbatim — 'meaning, you are one of those who are affected by witchcraft' — while the mind-loss element is correctly moved to al-Muyassar, whose text is exactly that: 'من الذين أصابهم السحر إصابة شديدة، فذهب بعقولهم'. al-Tabari's alternate reading also verbatim: 'إنما أنت يا شعيب معلل تعلل بالطعام والشراب، كما نعلل بهما، ولست ملكا'. Three editions named, none misattributed, no 'all four' claim. PROTECTED COUNTS RE-CHECKED AND ALL HOLD: musahhar (Form II) occurs in the entire Qur'an exactly twice, 26:153 and 26:185, both in this surah, 32 ayahs apart; mashur occurs exactly 4x across 3 surahs — 15:15, 17:47, 17:101, 25:8, i.e. twice inside al-Isra'; the refrain 'inna fi dhalika la-ayatan wa ma kana aktharuhum mu'minin' occurs exactly 8x, all in surah 26, at 8, 67, 103, 121, 139, 158, 174, 190 — matching the file's list exactly; and each of the three frame lines lands exactly 5x, all inside 106-180 (ala tattaqun at 106/124/142/161/177; inni lakum rasulun amin at 107/125/143/162/178; the no-wage line at 109/127/145/164/180) — confirming that the Musa and Ibrahim sections carry none of them. Also verified: zullah singular occurs only at 7:171 and 26:189; the plural occurs 4 more times (2:210, 31:32, 39:16 twice); and jibillan kathiran is at 36:62 only.
